accounting.rationale: Limits the retention guarantee using 19.5.2.5(6); SAVE on a pointer does not keep an unsaved target alive. Undefined association has no portable direct inquiry oracle.
Retain the 19.5.2.5(7) target-undefinition exception. Keeping the pointer object does not retain an unsaved BLOCK target or extend the identifier's scope.

Normative attribute-conferral rule: SAVE on the common block gives SAVE to every entity in it. The entity-retention and common-association operations keep their canonical owners; no duplicate BIND-common program or no-op S classifier is created.
The antecedent is the block's having SAVE, including a valid implication such as 8.5.5p3, not necessarily a SAVE spelling on each object.
Every conforming common-block entity receives the attribute. C8123/C8124 still restrict what can be a common member; a procedure pointer or allocatable does not become admissible by this sentence.
Attribute conferral is not explicit specification on the member. C862 can forbid SAVE x for a common member while SAVE /block/ correctly confers SAVE on it.

First sentence is the normative implicit-attribute definition and confirmation permission; the second is the conditional cross-scope common-block restriction. Fine units retain all three entity categories and all three exempt scopes.

The entity is declared in the stated scoping unit. A merely USE/host-accessed identifier, nested procedure local, interface-body entity or BLOCK local is not silently reclassified as declared in the containing main/module/submodule scope.
Variables in the stated scopes implicitly have SAVE; local-variable retention elsewhere remains p1/p2 with their exact conditions.
Common blocks in the stated scopes implicitly have SAVE; p3 conferral and the separate cross-scope antecedent remain distinct.
Procedure pointers in the stated scopes implicitly have SAVE. Their association, interface and host-lifetime semantics retain 15.4/15.6 and 19.5.2 ownership.
Direct declaration in a main-program scoping unit supplies the attribute. No post-image-termination value or storage-address observation is proposed.
Direct module declaration supplies SAVE. It does not give SAVE to every unsaved local in a contained subprogram.
Direct submodule declaration supplies SAVE. A submodule's being distinct from a module for C856 does not remove this explicit SAVE scope alternative.

Normative attribute implication, not a no-op execution or an inferred byte layout. Pending canonical declaration/initial-target relationships are documented in the view without authoring source-use instances or duplicate programs.

A legal explicit specification may confirm implicit SAVE. Respect C815/C862/C893, common-block rather than member specification, and 14.2.2p9's ban on respecifying an imported entity. This does not make two explicit specifications legal.

requirements.title: SAVE applies to a common block, variable or procedure pointer
requirements.definition: An entity with SAVE must be a common block, a variable or a procedure pointer. The category permission does not waive C862's explicit-specification exclusions or the declaration/statement grammar.

pending.ordinary-variable: PENDING compile/positive-control: a complete subprogram has ordinary fixed-type local INTEGER, constant-bound array, data-pointer and allocatable declarations with SAVE, each specified once and without initialization when isolating explicit SAVE. No dummy, result, automatic object or explicit saved common member.
pending.procedure-pointer: PENDING compile/positive-control: complete abstract interface and PROCEDURE(interface), POINTER declaration, with SAVE specified once either in that declaration or a SAVE statement. PROCEDURE supplies EXTERNAL; preserve C894 and 15.4.3.6. Do not invoke an unassociated pointer or infer that its internal-procedure target's host lives longer.
pending.named-common-block: PENDING compile/positive-control: ordinary INTEGER common members in a named block, SAVE /block/ on the block, no SAVE on individual members, no initializer and no forbidden common-member category. Use complete consistent declarations in any other participating scopes. Do not invent SAVE // syntax for blank common.
pending.named-constant-excluded: PENDING compile diagnostic/control: a complete subprogram declares INTEGER, PARAMETER :: k=3 then explicitly SAVE k. Remove PARAMETER, retaining the initializer and single SAVE specification, for a variable control. Require a SAVE-entity-category report, not a type/initializer/unknown-name error; ordinary procedure-name forms also retain the separate C894 owner.

requirements.oracle: Admit the three allowed categories and require source-attributed numbered reporting of the excluded constant with an accepted minimal repair. Reporting capability is not fatal rejection, a printed C861 token or a mandated message.
requirements.oracle_limitation: No compile-only admission establishes retained runtime state. Initialized variables, procedure-pointer initialization and enclosing-scope implication can already supply SAVE, so absence of the keyword is not an unsaved control. COMMON and procedure-pointer grammar retain their own owners.

requirements.title: SAVE is not explicitly specified for dummies, results, automatic objects or common members
requirements.source: 8.5.16 C862 and its four excluded entity classes; J3/24-007, physical PDF132.
requirements.definition: SAVE must not be specified for a dummy argument, a function result, an automatic data object or an object in a common block. This concerns specification on the excluded entity; SAVE on the common block can confer the attribute on its members, and a listless SAVE statement names only allowed items under 8.6.14p1.

pending.dummy-argument: PENDING compile diagnostic/control: complete module subroutine with a typed ordinary scalar dummy carrying SAVE, without initialization or other forbidden attributes. Delete SAVE only; use a complete matching interface and ordinary defined actual if a caller is included.
pending.function-result: PENDING compile diagnostic/control: complete function with a distinct RESULT(answer) name, ordinary INTEGER result declaration and SAVE answer, followed by definition of answer in executable code. Delete SAVE only. Do not accidentally test the external procedure name rather than its result variable.
pending.automatic-array-bound: PENDING canonical-owner/representation gate: nonoptional prior-typed INTEGER dummy n determines an ordinary local a(n) with explicit SAVE and no initializer/coarray/COMMON. Removing SAVE or changing the specification expression to a genuine constant repairs it; passing a constant or zero actual does not make n a constant expression. Existing C814 explicit-bound diagnostic/control cases retain 8.3/C814 ownership. No duplicate source, retagging or unsupported numbered-target link is authorized.
pending.automatic-character-length: PENDING canonical-owner/representation gate: local CHARACTER length determined by a nonconstant prior-typed n, using selector and entity-length forms, with explicit SAVE but no initializer. Delete SAVE or make the length expression constant. Preserve existing C814 character-selector/entity pairs, predicates and roles; zero runtime length is still automatic if the specification expression is nonconstant.
pending.common-member: PENDING compile diagnostic/control: ordinary INTEGER x in COMMON /shared/ x, followed by SAVE x in a complete nonmodule subprogram. Replace the SAVE operand x with /shared/ for a conforming block-level specification, keeping all participating scopes consistent. No initializer, allocatable, procedure pointer, coarray or unsupported common member is introduced.
pending.bare-save-eligibility-control: PENDING source-use/canonical-control gate: inspect the existing C814_valid__automatic_save_bare_save complete subprogram; its listless SAVE coexists with automatic CHARACTER(len=n) because only allowed items receive SAVE. It stays C814/positive-control/compile. Do not turn this into a C862 negative or add an explicit SAVE specification alongside the bare SAVE contrary to C893.
pending.constant-local-control: PENDING source-use/canonical-control gate: existing C814 parameter/LEN/SIZE constant-specification controls demonstrate nonautomatic local declarations. Preserve their IDs, roles and complete sources; a new C862 representation requires coordinator review rather than copied programs or silently credited facets.

requirements.oracle: For new isolated dummy/result/common-member cases require standard numbered reporting and accepted minimal repairs. Automatic-object cases share their semantic prohibition with existing C814; their primary ownership and causal byte/predicate contracts must be preserved. The current canonical-link target is supplementary, not an arbitrary numbered target, so this overlap remains a precise pending mechanism decision.
requirements.oracle_limitation: C814 is in 8.3, not the explicit-shape syntax subclause. Do not add initialization to an automatic, dummy or result negative: C808 would supply another cause. Implicit main/module/submodule SAVE does not license explicit SAVE on a common member or a nested procedure's dummy/result. Empty-value definedness is not automatic-object or SAVE eligibility.

requirements.title: Saved local variables retain the specified state across RETURN or END and are shared across subprogram instances
requirements.source: 8.5.16 p1, both sentences and the pointer-target exception; J3/24-007, physical PDF132.
requirements.definition: A saved local variable of a program unit or subprogram retains its association status, allocation status, definition status and value after RETURN or END, except for a pointer whose target becomes undefined under 19.5.2.5(6). A local variable of a subprogram with SAVE is shared by every instance of that subprogram. SAVE does not initially define an otherwise undefined variable or extend a target lifetime.

pending.return-defined-values: PENDING bounded run/effect: complete main and explicit-interface subroutine with a local INTEGER, SAVE variable and no declaration initializer. Caller supplies phases 1,2,3; phase1 defines 11, phase2 checks 11 and stores 17, phase3 checks 17. Each invocation explicitly RETURNs and publishes ordinary snapshots/visit counts; main independently verifies literals and completion. No read precedes the first definition.
pending.end-defined-values: PENDING bounded run/effect or canonical-reuse gate: normal END SUBROUTINE completion is distinct from an explicit RETURN path. The existing S7_5_4_6_009_valid__initialization_save_contrast is a candidate with independent 3 then 9 checks on its explicitly saved local across two visits; preserve its S7.5.4.6-009/effect ownership and review the full connection instead of cloning it. A separate direct design would use defined reentry values and complete visits. No post-END PROGRAM observation or storage address is an oracle.
pending.live-data-pointer-association: PENDING bounded run/effect: explicitly saved local data pointer is associated during the first invocation with a defined, nonempty scalar module TARGET that remains live. After complete return/reentry, require ASSOCIATED(pointer,target), known payload 11, and an independent target mutation to 17 observed on a later call. No dummy-target lifetime ambiguity, undefined-status query or assumed representation.
pending.defined-disassociated-pointer: PENDING bounded run/effect: an explicitly saved local data pointer is unconditionally NULLIFYed before the first return, and a later invocation safely requires one-argument ASSOCIATED to be false. Use independent phase/visit observers. Defined disassociation is not undefined association and does not authorize a pointee read.
pending.allocated-object-retention: PENDING bounded run/effect: explicitly saved local allocatable INTEGER array starts unallocated, is allocated with two elements and defined as [11,13] on phase1, then remains allocated across return/reentry with guarded shape and literal payload checks. Modify to [17,19] for a further complete call. No OUT argument, explicit intervening deallocation or finalizable type confounds this ordinary retention case.
pending.unallocated-status-retention: PENDING bounded run/effect: explicitly saved allocatable remains unallocated on the first two complete entries and ALLOCATED is false without SIZE/LBOUND/data inquiry. A later controlled allocation and definition provides a nonvacuous contrast, with entry/completion guards. Do not conflate zero size, zero character length or absent optional arguments with this status.
pending.allocated-empty-status: PENDING bounded run/effect: after observing initial unallocated status, allocate a saved rank-one INTEGER array of size zero; return and reenter, then require ALLOCATED true before SIZE zero. The status transition, not nonexistent elements or always-defined empty data alone, is observed. No hidden empty lower bound or address is asserted.
pending.shared-recursive-instances: PENDING bounded run/effect: one complete RECURSIVE subprogram declares a saved local INTEGER without a declaration initializer. Outer depth initializes 11, inner depth observes 11 and changes it to 17, and the still-active outer instance observes 17 after the inner return. Use separate ordinary dummy snapshots/visit counters and depth guards, not an aliased dummy for the saved object. Sequential calls alone do not demonstrate simultaneous-instance sharing.

requirements.oracle: Read only state established before the completed event and observed on a valid later entry. Independently specified literals, association identity, allocation-before-dependent-inquiry guards, visits and completion must distinguish missing calls or no-op paths. All future effects require unchanged conforming parents and qualified full-program sensitivity/actual-mode evidence; none is supplied by this source packet.
requirements.oracle_limitation: There is no portable direct assertion that an undefined variable remains undefined. Retaining undefined/disassociated association never authorizes dereference or an undefined ASSOCIATED inquiry. Procedure-pointer eligibility and saved-entity/host-lifetime semantics retain C861, 15.4.3.6, 15.6.2.4 and 19.5.2 ownership; do not silently replace p1's variable subject with arbitrary entities. SAVE is not an absence-of-all-finalization oracle and does not defeat explicit deallocation, INTENT(OUT) or assignment events.

requirements.title: Saved BLOCK locals retain the specified state across termination and are shared across containing subprogram instances
requirements.source: 8.5.16 p2, both sentences and the pointer-target exception; J3/24-007, physical PDF132.
requirements.definition: A saved local variable of a BLOCK retains its association status, allocation status, definition status and value after the construct terminates, except for a pointer whose target becomes undefined under 19.5.2.5(7). If that BLOCK is within a subprogram, the variable is shared by all instances of the subprogram. Retained storage does not extend the name's scope.

pending.same-block-defined-values: PENDING bounded run/effect: execute the same lexical BLOCK in three controlled iterations. A local INTEGER, SAVE without declaration initialization is first defined as 11, then checked and changed to 17, then checked again. Export ordinary snapshots before each END BLOCK and verify independent outer visit/completion counters. Never read the BLOCK name outside its scope or confuse equal names in different BLOCKs.
pending.block-live-pointer-association: PENDING bounded run/effect: first activation associates an explicitly saved BLOCK-local data pointer with a defined nonempty TARGET that lives outside the BLOCK for every activation. Later activation checks ASSOCIATED to that target and a known payload. The target is not an unsaved object that died with the previous BLOCK.
pending.block-disassociated-pointer: PENDING bounded run/effect: first activation unconditionally NULLIFYs the saved pointer; a later activation checks false ASSOCIATED without data dereference. Independent iteration/entry markers prevent skipping the tested activation; undefined association is excluded.
pending.block-allocated-status: PENDING bounded run/effect: saved BLOCK-local allocatable array is allocated and defined as [11,13] in the first activation and, after END BLOCK, is checked allocated before size/data inquiries on the next activation. Change its data to [17,19] for another activation and publish literal-checked snapshots inside scope.
pending.block-unallocated-status: PENDING bounded run/effect: explicitly saved allocatable is observed unallocated at two valid activations, then deliberately allocated in a later one for a contrasting state. Use only ALLOCATED while unallocated and retain independent iteration/completion observers.
pending.block-allocated-empty: PENDING bounded run/effect: saved allocatable changes from unallocated to allocated size zero inside the BLOCK and retains that status on reentry. Require ALLOCATED before SIZE; always-defined empty values alone do not establish SAVE, allocation or presence.
pending.block-shared-subprogram-instances: PENDING bounded run/effect: a complete RECURSIVE subprogram reenters the same lexical BLOCK while the outer instance remains active. Outer defines its saved scalar as 11, inner observes 11 and stores 17, outer then checks 17. Separate snapshots and visit counters retain exact instances and prevent a sequential-only or different-BLOCK proxy.

requirements.oracle: Observe each retained state only while the same BLOCK's scope is active, publishing defined snapshots to the controller before termination. Source-independent literals and full entry/exit/completion observers are required. The source distinguishes termination of a BLOCK from RETURN/END of a procedure and from termination of the image.
requirements.oracle_limitation: An unsaved target can die even when the pointer is saved; reset or re-associate before any later inquiry if that exception applies. Do not observe a dead target, use addresses, assume component/default initialization implies SAVE, or claim missing finalizer output alone establishes these retention effects. Existing saved-block finalization controls retain 7.5.6.3 ownership.

requirements.title: SAVE on a common block in a nonexempt scope requires SAVE in every nonexempt declaring scope
requirements.source: 8.5.16 p4, second sentence, including antecedent and all three scope exclusions; J3/24-007, physical PDF132.
requirements.definition: If a common block has SAVE in any scoping unit other than a main program, module or submodule, it must have SAVE in every scoping unit declaring that block that is not one of those three kinds. The test is whether the block has the attribute, not whether a SAVE keyword is present. Implicit SAVE solely in an exempt scope does not by itself satisfy this nonexempt antecedent.

pending.all-nonexempt-scopes-saved: PENDING compile/positive-control: complete main plus two ordinary external writer/reader subprograms declare the same named nonempty COMMON with identical default-INTEGER layout and SAVE /block/ in both actual common scopes. Main's snapshots are separate ordinary variables; write before any read. This is a uniformity control, not a new retained-value effect or duplicate of BIND-common.
pending.missing-other-scope-save: PENDING optional-diagnostic-policy/source-use gate: the same complete named-COMMON program gives SAVE only in one external subprogram, with no BIND or other implication in the other. The minimal repair adds SAVE /block/ to the missing scope. Do not execute the nonconforming variant for a mandated failure or infer required whole-program diagnosis from this prose shall.
pending.implicit-only-exempt-scope-control: PENDING compile/positive-control: a main-program or module declaration has implicit SAVE on the named common block, while two other complete external declarations have no SAVE, BIND or other SAVE implication. The nonexempt antecedent is false. Keep storage sequences/type parameters conforming and all reads preceded by definition; active common storage is not evidence of a separate SAVE retention effect.
pending.mixed-exempt-scopes: PENDING compile/positive-control: complete main/module/legitimate-submodule and ordinary external declarations of one named COMMON use matching ordinary INTEGER storage sequences. Give SAVE in every nonexempt declaring scope; no extra SAVE statement is required in main/module/submodule. Distinguish direct declarations from contained procedure or interface scopes and avoid passing common members as aliased defining dummies.
pending.bind-implied-save-candidate: PENDING canonical-role gate: both existing S8.5.5-002 programs give the block BIND(C) in the actual external writer/reader scopes, so both already have SAVE under 8.5.5p3. Their retention effect and explicit-SAVE positive-control roles stay unchanged. Removing a SAVE spelling from the confirmation program does not create this rule's missing-attribute negative; no clone, retag, link or control opt-in is authored.
pending.bare-save-antecedent: PENDING compile/positive-control plus separate optional-policy negative gate: in a nonexempt scope containing the named common block, a sole listless SAVE gives SAVE to allowed items. Other nonexempt declarations must then have SAVE too. Repair a missing scope with a named-block SAVE statement; respect C893 and never combine blanket SAVE with additional SAVE specifications in the same scope.

requirements.oracle: Compare complete cross-scope declarations and actual attribute implications before proposing a diagnostic. Valid controls preserve matching COMMON layouts and legal execution if reached. A future negative needs its own policy or independently demonstrated numbered/scope reporting basis and a same-program minimal repair; no arbitrary runtime result or generic link failure is an oracle.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Bound the proposed contrasts to named nonempty common blocks. Blank common's nonpointer retention follows its separate 8.10.2.5/19.6.6 rules and is not proof of SAVE or a license for SAVE // syntax. BIND, initialization rules and scope implication cannot be ignored when judging whether SAVE is absent. The existing canonical-link schema does not approve these source/use relationships automatically.

Retained association/allocation/definition/value obey actual RETURN/END/BLOCK events, recursion and live-target premises. Implicit main/module/submodule SAVE, explicit initialization, DATA exceptions, default initialization and BIND routes stay distinct. Common-block SAVE confers attributes through the block while C862 forbids member specification; the cross-scope obligation retains its nonexempt antecedent. Blank-common retention is not a SAVE declaration. Existing BIND-common effect/control and initialization/finalization/entry-capture evidence retain owners and roles.
